reviews.text: Portman and Moore are excellent, but Melton is the revelation in a satire that targets method actors and cheesy true crime adaptations equally well. Haynes use of mirrors is immaculate, as is the utterly ridiculous melodramatic score.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The screenplay by Samy Burch is almost creepily polite, with Elizabeth saying thank you to Gracie and her family dozens of times; there's lots of papering over various deceits and self-delusions.
reviews.author: Jen Shieff

reviews.text: A combination of rollicking, darkly delicious entertainment and brilliantly rendered character study, this has the making of a modern classic.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: All in all, May December proves to be a compelling film, one that invites the audience to look beneath the surface and sit with the uncomfortable truth we may find there.
reviews.author: Clotilde Chinnici

reviews.text: To the viewer, May December presents broken characters riddled with variations of pain and guilt, leaving it up to those watching what forgiveness or acceptance they deserve.
reviews.author: Yasmine Kandil

reviews.text: Simmering and summering, Haynes’ take is as much implication as demonstration, a variation on tabloid material that makes bittersweet and sinister and aromatic flavors, like the great distillations in twentieth-century Atom Egoyan.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman are acting titans but Charles Melton becomes the film’s breakthrough performance.
reviews.author: Nelson Acosta

reviews.text: May December takes what we know about the trope of the blonde/brunette doppelgänger and uses it to tell a story about telling a story.
reviews.author: Kayla McCulloch

reviews.text: This movie is serving THEMES. Why does Hollywood love to look for the humanity in bad people? Can a person truly live a life without regret?
reviews.author: Jessica Baxter

reviews.text: May December is wickedly funny on the subject of delusion and the lies we tell ourselves to get what we want, but always there is Joe, the painful reminder of the human cost of those lies and delusions.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Delicate hothouse dramedy around a core of three fantastic actors.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: With May December, Haynes returns to the fully immersive horror of Safe while also braiding paradoxically dramatic and hilarious tones — I believe what I’m seeing even as I’m laughing at the outrageousness of the whole scenario.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Melton comes out of nowhere and hints that a better movie would have focused on Joe. Melton adds a complex pathos to Joe, who claims not to be a victim, but is alone at sea with no safe person to process his emotions over his predicament.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Nothing in May December is what it seems. The film unravels in the high-strung beats of a melodrama (Marcelo Zarvos’ music amping up the stakes) but embedded within are revelations fit for a slow-burn horror story.
reviews.author: Ishita Sengupta

reviews.text: May December is not just a skilful satire of suburban propriety; it’s a unique and uncanny affair about the nature of performance itself.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: Alarming film with a poisonous view of drama. An equally brilliant companion piece to Haynes's Safe, from 1995, May December identifies and measures the new surfaces of banality that have emerged in our lives in the intervening twenty-eight years.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: A fascinating interpretation of a true story, which uses an interesting balance of tones —altering between the absolutely serious and the trashy— and which makes the most of the talents of its spectacular main actors and actresses. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Haynes makes the most of Moore... but also of Melton who puts himself at the center of the story naturally and extraordinarily, embodying all the complexity of a character trapped in circumstances that have confused his identity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pedro Gallego

reviews.text: It takes a deft hand to blend the true crime–inspired elements of this subject with moments of twisted humor.
reviews.author: Julianna Ress

reviews.text: May December is a film rich with intricate layers, occasionally posing challenges in unravelling its depth.
reviews.author: Abhishek Srivastava

reviews.text: The film is supported by the talent of two phenomenal actresses, Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman, but also by meticulous staging, loaded with mirror images and symmetrical reflections... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Lingenti

reviews.text: The tone constantly walks a tightrope that keeps the viewer off balance, forcing them to ask themselves at every turn if they are empathizing with anyone on screen. If so, with whom, why, and whether the pursuit of motivations is really relevant.
reviews.author: Valentina Morillo

reviews.text: Mirror shots recur often in May December, a movie with characters yet so incapable of self reflection.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: May December is not afraid... it moves away from solemnity, political correctness, and prestige to embrace its uninhibited and provocative spirit. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Haynes is a master of the impossible melodrama. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: A stylistic and moral puzzle. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: The murky story could be fascinating, but Todd Haynes's way of telling it makes it insignificant, and unavainlingly pretentious. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: Todd Haynes' new film is an ironic and tortured x-ray of abuse, immaturity, and falsehood. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: This tale unpacks the idea of love between a child and an adult, and makes it clear that no amount of reframing can hide the hideous inequalities.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Engrossing, prickly and thought-provoking.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: The (melo)drama is served in an entertaining (even funny) and apparently, though it is not, a superficial way. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: How ambiguous can our identity be? [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: May December is a delicious, acting masterclass that equally seduces its audience with  flirtatious appeal
reviews.author: Latoya Austin

reviews.text: If our sympathies are with Elizabeth at the beginning of the film as she tries to crack Gracie’s mask of forced positivity, by the end we’ve learned to mistrust her motivations.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: ... An almost Lynchian look at the biases inherent in the stories we tell, an examination of the perils and pitfalls of making a biopic and the personalised nature of what is “the truth”.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: The two women are astonishingly good here, but at least as good is Charles Melton...
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Melton’s heart-rending performance as the collateral damage wreaked by the actions of both women who walks away with the film.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Haynes fabricates a narrative that, between reflections and shadows, brings to light a scandal and then rearranges it among other reflections and other shadows. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: In the end, the best thing about this film is watching this tête à tête between Moore and Portman, engaged in a perverse mirroring game, deceptively simple and delicate, from which the B side of this scandalous story emerges. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: Three big protagonists make this film a perverse game of mirrors in which no one, not even the viewer, can safely leave. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Jose Cruz

reviews.text: Melodrama and a generous helping of dark comedy combine in this compelling character study from Todd Haynes, which manages to be hilarious and heartfelt all at once.
reviews.author: Jamie Dunn

reviews.text: May December plays out like one of these 3D pictures you need to unfocus your eyes to see, revealing more only after it is all taken in.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: Complex, intelligent, thought-provoking filmmakers are back in fashion.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Both performances are built out of distancing devices, and the whole film is shot through with camp irony, though the effect, as usual with Haynes, is more conceptual than outright funny.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: An unnerving reimagining of a notorious relationship from director Todd Haynes is a conduit for unanswerable questions.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: This is a thoughtful and compassionate movie, beautifully portrayed, when it could have been something very different.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Moore and Portman are both in compelling form here, but their dynamic displays won’t be enough to seal the deal for all viewers.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: There’s a bit of Tennessee Williams in May December...
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: May December is a very glossy psychological portrait of manipulation and exploitation, inspired by a real-life sex scandal. Although the principal cast members give above-average performances, it's a slow-moving film with a fragmented story.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Haynes’s default juke, sometimes so subtly played you can miss it, is an earnest engagement with genre while simultaneously sprinkling sand in its gears, so its malfunctioning becomes a cool-eyed critique of genre presumptions.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: I truly believe that Todd Haynes is the only director on this planet who could have successfully made this into a comedy. Or, for that matter, made this at all.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: May December is salacious and insidious. Misrepresenting real life, it is a transgressive act of criminal reprieve.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The acting in this film is superb by the whole cast, and the screenplay by Samy Burch and Alex Mechanik is very clever indeed, weaving together different stories and different genres. This is one of the best movies by acclaimed director Todd Haynes.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The film features good performances by Natalie Portman, Julianne Moore and Charles Melton, but while Melton's character breaks the stereotype of East Asian men not being attractive, there are no signs of his cultural heritage.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: At times humorous but always disturbing, May December is among the greatest psychological dramas of the decade so far. It is almost certain to become a "cult classic", so make sure you've seen it before you fall behind during haute holiday matinee banter.
reviews.author: Ana Yorke

reviews.text: Director Todd Haynes’ subversive pastiche finds a great deal of sincerity in Charles Melton’s revelatory performance.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: There are intriguing and subtle observations here about the self-centeredness of certain social layers, but not much more.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: …there are no winners here; Gracie and Elizabeth are self-seeking characters who don’t feel any moral responsibility for past or present, and that lack of any real moral compass should encourage audiences to reflect and self-select before watching this….
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: This uneven examination of fame and manipulation has trouble finding its focus.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Todd Haynes’s discomfiting and hypnotic suburban melodrama examines topics the director knows well: sex, taboo, and control.
reviews.author: Beatrice Loayza

reviews.text: A brilliant addition to a specialized genre of films.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: The film is so deft in its footing... I thought it was terrific.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman are both outstanding. Charles Melton, whose character speaks his mind with quiet assurance, is Oscar-worthy as Joe. Director Haynes builds “May December” like a superbly crafted puzzle.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Alternately darkly funny and profoundly sad, May December feels like a movie only Haynes could have made — and made so masterfully.
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: It is an attempt at cleverness, but it comes across as smug and the over all tone is too artsy for its own good. Now every actor involved is gifted... but there are several odd choices that are made that make may December very unappealing.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Melton's performance sets the film's emotional rhythms alongside the musical score from Marcelo Zarvos.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: The stories we tell — in movies and to ourselves — are explored and exploded in “May December,” director Todd Haynes’ fascinating drama about the blurry line between truth and reality.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: May December is a disturbing portrait of abuse, and a campy parody of performance.
reviews.author: Ella Feldman

reviews.text: Genre is elastic, people! This is a potent, pitch black satire that skewers, flirts with and ultimately circumvents histrionic melodrama--often scene by scene, to delirious effect.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Haynes builds up the drama throughout May December with his most effective devices. Each character embraces their purpose in ways that subconsciously carry viewers through the story with simple actions but complicated motives.
reviews.author: Sabina Dana Plasse

reviews.text: "May December" feels like the movie version of attempting to euphemize the word pedophile with the term "minor-attracted." Charles Melton turns in his best performance to date.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Haynes has once again excelled with a very original film, giving an inspired treatment to throny material to deliver a story with rich characters he never tries to judge, but rather display their miseries, selfishness and virtues. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Milton Calopiña

reviews.text: While some questions can only be answered by individuals, it is clear that Todd Haynes is in complete control, and sitting in his passenger seat is thrilling.
reviews.author: Howard Waldstein

reviews.text: Haynes's melodrama remains situated in an accommodating horizon that, strictly speaking, lacks the emotional pulse to deeply interrogate his specific commentary on sexual abuse and the actor's task to emulate identities. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: May December is a film that will burrow itself beneath your skin. At first glance, it appears to be a trashy and melodramatic portrayal of a couple who sparked a media frenzy. However, digging deeper uncovers a psychological tale about human depravity...
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: ...a slow-paced yet mostly compelling drama...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: On one hand too superficial, and on the other not very mysterious, May December is the type of film in which you don't want to get involved once the credits start rolling. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: There’s a lurid, made-for-t.v. movie quality that gives the film a wicked streak that’s both tongue-in-cheek and deliciously potent.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: “May December” isn’t the “ripped from the headlines” story you might want. But it is one you should stop to consider.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: The premise alone, with its connections to a real-life story, is potentially controversial, but Haynes handles it with confidence and manages to spin it into a thoughtful, insightful and most importantly, wildly entertaining film.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The film relates deeply to Edward Hopper's view on loneliness. Like the paintings, the film is a clear and delicate window to observe upon it: physical, mental, and, above all, spiritual. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: It is at once a film of immense complexity and immense clarity.
reviews.author: Drew Gregory

reviews.text: It all seems superficial - beautifully superficial - but superficial all the way.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: With moments of humor and others that reflect horror Haynes manages to immerse us in the depths of his characters, capturing both their innocence and perversity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: Ultimately, the audience is left with the sensation that there is much more to uncover - something distorted and concealed beneath the apparent restraint of inscrutable emotions.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Maybe the most excruciatingly brilliant takedown of method acting since Tropic Thunder?
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Todd Haynes is a filmmaker who, on top of telling a story about vulnerable people and their digressions, tells the story about the predatory ways we consume those narratives, and the boundaries we cross when creating those narratives.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: A drama that gets under your skin and plays out like a thriller in places, May December is a shocking watch that puts character development at the forefront to create an addictive and intoxicating watch.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: Sad, sordid riff on what may have happened to that 36 year-old schoolteacher who had an affair with a seventh grade student - and how the arrival of a TV star, portraying her, changed their lives. Natalie Portman's mimicry of Julianne Moore is remarkable.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Every scene between Portman and Moore shivers with a delicate sort of tension.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Todd Haynes’s latest is a brilliant ode to female toxicity that begins at a place of camp and ends at one that’s closer to horror.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text:
Todd Haynes has crafted the best movie of 2023. 
Mind-blowing.
If ever there was, or is, a filmic antidote to the corporate gaslighting garbage that a movie such as "Barbie" represents, "May December" is it. 
Prepare to be transformed.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: In the end, May December offers neither the campy juice you get from those ripped-from-the-headlines TV movies it mocks or the depths of a psychological art film like Ingmar Bergman’s Persona.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: Whatever May December is, it’s not for me. Filled with only one or two non-hot-dog-related moments of levity that I could identify, calling this a comedy is like referring to a fall down an elevator shaft as “a wild ride.” I suppose?
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: A movie made by smart people, but it feels half-digested.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Todd Haynes expertly weaves melodrama like nobody else and this is the hottest gas he's ever cooked with.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: The only thing that can be cut with a knife is the tension, which [director Todd] Haynes masterfully handles, laying down each coating upon the audience until we're up to our neck in emotional strain.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: While there’s nothing outright graphic or gruesome happening on screen, May December is unbearable. The false sense of breeziness is actually stiflingly heavy.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Intentional humor and strategic moments of relief, supported by an overwhelming soundtrack, balance the tension and make the film addictive. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Pablo Russo

reviews.text: Film’s heart and soul belong to Charles Melton as Moore’s husband, some 30 years her junior and forever trapped in the shadow of scandal...
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: May December is my favorite kind of exploration in this vein -- a thoroughly “human story” that asks the questions that true crime begs, without pretending to know the answers.
reviews.author: Alison Lanier

reviews.text: May December, in addition to diagnosing the rotten core of our era’s most popular entertainment, becomes a tragedy about aging—drifting further and further from yourself, until you're yet another subject to study, scrutinize, and completely misunderstand.
reviews.author: Paul Thompson

reviews.text: With shades of Alfred Hitchcock and Ingmar Bergman’s Persona, May December keeps viewers guessing and off-kilter, but in a good way. The film is subtle, strange and riv­eting; a heady mix of irresistible but uneasy entertainment.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: All the acting here is extraordinary, but there’s a reason why Charles Melton has been picking some early awards hardware for his role as Joe.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: The movie becomes very twisty as Natalie Portman [her character] becomes more involved in their [Moore & Melton's characters] lives.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: Slyly scripted, this film uncovers a horrifying peak at the mind a child abuser and the harrowingly sad consequences for the victim.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: Overall, May December isn’t really all that memorable or compelling. It’s just a movie about a messed-up situation that’s elevated by outstanding performances.
reviews.author: Lissete Lanuza Sáenz

reviews.text: A thorny, unsettling piece of work, beautiful to look at but just as uncomfortable to contemplate.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: May December is a masterfully crafted exploration of complex relationships, featuring standout performances and a gripping narrative. A must-see.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Spearheaded by a trio of visceral, mesmerizing performances from Natalie Portman, Julianne Moore, and Charles Melton, May December is a paradoxically heartbreaking exploration of trauma wrapped up in a sharp wit.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: A gripping character study.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Challenging, but extremely entertaining. Difficult to explain, but easy to understand. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Santisteban

reviews.text: Often ridiculous and occasionally devastating.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: “May December” is a dark, unsettling drama with nervy comic undertones. It’s smart, but frustratingly uneven.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Anchored by Moore and Portman’s “mother-off” warfare, Melton’s breathtaking performance, and Burch’s expertly toned screenplay, Todd Haynes' May December is remarkable.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: A masterpiece of cringe with small lines of dialogue or subtle glances that make your skin crawl.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: May December is a force of a film because of the acting throughout it, with Charles Milton delivering one of the most riveting and emotional performances of the year.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Haynes lets us sit in the truth of the situation. No matter what occurred in the past, there’s still considerable tension to explore in each relationship. How he exploits those tensions is what makes Haynes a master.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: It's a movie with many layers, spanning generations and motivations, that bears thinking about and certainly re-watching.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: There’s nothing comedic about May December despite it being billed as such.
reviews.author: Lori Meek

reviews.text: Todd Haynes’s May December is a demented, fever dream-esque Nancy Meyers film full of deviously delicious performances by its three stars and a slick script from Samy Burch.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Todd Haynes also uses symbolism & beautiful photography as a commentary on love, hysteria, passion and an outside world that keeps judging. Biggest surprise was Charles Melton, compelling as Joe in a slow emergence from larvae to butterfly. Portman rises!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Haynes is a master of winking provocation, and you can almost hear him giggling with delight as he directs... to find pseudo-cordial, deeply chilly and profoundly awkward air to share as each character tries to suss out the other’s intentions.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The performances make May December a captivating viewing experience. Charles Melton especially gives a career-making performance. It’s not easy for an up-and-coming actor to stand out while acting next to powerhouses Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore.
reviews.author: Jerrica Tisdale

reviews.text: Haynes has made a beautiful, terrible nesting doll of a film with a uniquely twisted core. Beneath the droll portrait of an actor’s obsession with her muse is an unsettling tale of what happens when people refuse to tell the truth.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: Todd Hayne’s May December takes a lurid page from recent pop history and turns it into a troubling deep dive into bruised and battered psyches.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: May December is like a Lifetime movie that’s fallen into enemy hands.
reviews.author: Tom Gliatto

reviews.text: It gets just so juicy and wrong and thrilling in darkly funny ways.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Really tightly put together, and and just so well acted.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: That Haynes gets at these characters in a way that Elizabeth only hopes to, is what makes the film so wickedly entertaining.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: The story of May December contains elements that will creep certain viewers out, whether it’s the subject matter itself or the performances of the two great lead actors.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: May December is a chilling portrayal of identity and how we all can lose ourselves in the drama.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Boasts three powerhouse performances. Starts out campy but by the end is truly heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The best role belongs to Portman, who will surely get major awards attention for her turn as ambitious, diligent and perpetually line-crossing Elizabeth.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: “May December” is one of the saddest and most provocative films of the year.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: It’s a pity because Julianne Moore, Natalie Portman and Charles Melton gave their all in May December but were ultimately defeated by a largely muted and hollow storytelling.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Melton delivers brilliantly. Haynes delivers provocative, noirish melodrama, beautifully nostalgic, creepy, sordid, and, if it weren’t so well done, mawkish.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: A remarkable cast.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: There’s nothing comedic about it to hail it a dark comedy. Yet, there’s insufficient depth to ground it in a poignant drama. We’re enticed but never thrilled.
reviews.author: Kit Stone

reviews.text: This is one of those films where every element must be firing on all cylinders to work. If one piece didn’t fit correctly, the entire puzzle would fall apart.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Natalie Portman is in top-notch form here and delivers one of the best performances of the year.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: There are instances when it seems as if you’re watching two overlaid movies: the original and its critique, a doubling that works nicely in “May December,” which soon becomes a labyrinthine hall of mirrors.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: May December is a satire of true crime and our fascination with tabloid criminality, of how the worst of human behavior can be exploited as entertainment, but mostly, it's a chance to watch a trio of great performances that draw us into this uneasy story.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A farcical black social comedy, Todd Haynes’s May December offers a catty and campy twist on Bergman’s Persona, satirizing Hollywood along the way.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: And while Haynes successfully updates his Douglas Sirkian-gaze by examining a modern version of domestic angst, I expected something more than just a restating of the obvious.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The film's most fascinating element is watching Portman and Moore's performances tangle and untangle themselves. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: There’s more than a little uncomfortable humor in this script. Brought to life with sharp performances from Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore, Todd Haynes’ direction of Samy Burch’s writing is one guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: It's Haynes' most accessible work of his career, and it's one of the year's best movies. It's a knockout in May, December, or anytime in between.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Viewers may find themselves laughing through this unsettling drama in a way that feels intentional by Haynes but also somewhat inappropriate, given the charged subject matter.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Moore and Portman inject the movie with wattage, dramatic heft, and a push-pull dynamic associated with immovable objects and irresistible forces. Melton gives May December its slow-burn tragedy. It’s why the film wounds the way it does.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: With some unusual psychological games at play, having Haynes deploying plenty of ways to be entertained allows these characters to really click.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A brilliant building and layering of characters.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: Tremendously well done. It does teeter on the edge of comedy, but it's a dramatic film to my mind.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: An electrifying slow-burn film about fame, trauma, and sensationalized scandals.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: Who benefits when crime is turned into entertainment? Everyone and no one. We are all perpetrators and victims, at least here.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: It's constantly on the precipice of something major happening, but nothing ever does. Even the score heightens as it tries to hint that the payoff is coming, but it never does. Leads do what they can with what they were given, but can't save this one.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Moore creates a complex character who appears the hallmark of grace and kindness, but actually proves unexpectedly manipulative, delivering cruelty with a smile.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: It’s uncomfortable, it’s off putting, it’s entirely illicit—and that’s why it works so well.
reviews.author: Laura Babiak

reviews.text: A hell of a film.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: Something striking is always on the verge of happening, yet it rarely does; even the music nearly laughably sets the stage for dramatic revelations that fizzle or remain unrealized.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: A troubling, somber study, but one shot through with dark, edgy humor that sneaks up on you.  The result is funny, unsettling and poignant by turns, but still feeling all of a piece rather than a disjointed composite.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Todd Haynes’ provocative drama is full of questions. After watching it, I’ve got a few of my own.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: May December is a thought-provoking, multilayered exploration of voyeuristic tabloid culture and a complex character study of a man whose childhood was taken away too soon. The film features three of the best performances of the year, especially Melton.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: Todd Haynes will make you feel for the characters long after the credits end.  See it with friends and then get ready to talk, argue, dream and scheme about where the characters go next.  There will be Oscar nominations. There should be Oscar wins.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: Haynes' two main characters provide twice as much opportunity to plunge the depths of human emotion and complex histories, and he does so in heartbreaking, fascinating ways.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: May December, Todd Hayne’s riveting, comic, yet poignant look at the ghoulish curiosity of the human mind, the blurring of lines between performance and feeling, and the moral red lines we cross to achieve our desires.
reviews.author: Ayelet Dekel

reviews.text: Applying a smattering of unlikely kinks and a confounding third act of insecurity swerves sinks the film. Haynes is left with a mood piece of examining taboo with more taboo. and it gets unattractively lost in just that very vibe.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Despite the high controversy of the central theme, the black comedy peeks shamelessly throughout the script co-written by Samy Burch and Alex Mechanik. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gustavo Herrera Taboada

reviews.text: Portman and Moore give sensitive, thoughtful performances in a Persona-like meditation on identity, agency, trauma, boundaries, and the gulf between the way we want to be seen and the need to be known for who we are.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: a gripping very femme-centric drama scripted by Samy Burch, directed by Todd Haynes and starring Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore as utterly fascinating women, revealing in turn their sparring personalities and counterpoint objectives.
reviews.author: Jennifer Merin

reviews.text: First time screenwriter, Samy Burch taps into a vibe of horror meets soap opera as she explores a May – December relationship that mimics that of Mary Kay Letourneau and Vili Fualaau’s illegal love affair and then lawful marriage from the late 1990’s.
reviews.author: T.J. Callahan

reviews.text: All three leads of May December know exactly the tone that Todd Haynes’ has set for them. It’s a fascinating probe taking the viewer on a different mindset then you’d expect from this story.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Todd Haynes' May December is about the ugliness that permeates human nature, and our leanings towards the salacious, practically ignoring the very real people at the centre of it all.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Portman and Moore deliver a master class in acting during every scene they inhabit. What becomes a case of opposites slowly turns into personalities melding together.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: If May December is meant to be a critique of media exploitation and the public’s voracious appetite for sexual scandal, it’s trying to have its cake and eat it too.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: And that’s Haynes’s film: two lionesses licking their lips while they apply each other’s make-up. It’s a strange film, a little chilly, veering between black comedy and zoned-out melodrama...
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: May December works best as a dark comedy, a portrait of the American suburbs hungry for gossip and cobblers but unwilling to grapple with tough conversations.
reviews.author: Justine Smith

reviews.text: Engaging and sincere as an exploration of what the artistic process even means in the face of strange human tragedy.
reviews.author: Joel Copling

reviews.text: Ultimately, it’s a work of art to be admired more than adored, and the end result is an emotionally hollow experience. But that’s not to say that it won’t make you chuckle at a host of characters oblivious to the irony of their actions.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: May December is a trick of a movie, and it doesn’t hide it.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Anybody looking for something off the beaten path - but not too off - will appreciate the subtle underlying humor and cleverly stylized performances.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Serpentine in its plotting, queasily unsettling in its subject matter, and very, very funny, Todd Haynes’s latest picture is as deft a tonal juggling act as you will see anywhere this year.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: It’s a little as if Bergman’s “Persona” had been remade by the Real Housewives of Savannah.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Much like the gossip-laden tabloids that spawned the latest from director Todd Haynes, his fifth screen collaboration with Julianne Moore flashes a clunky quality that works both for and against it.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Todd Haynes’ new movie is one nasty piece of fun...Funny, but quite vicious.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore lock horns in this small town melodrama, that see-saws between intimate character study and intriguing love triangle, propelled along by powerhouse performances.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: We’re left with plaguing questions that challenge what we hold dear: our entertainment, our source of empowerment, our safety.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: It unfortunately becomes muddled and can’t decide what it is trying to say
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The Joe-Gracie dynamic is like Gus Van Sant’s To Die For; the Elizabeth-Gracie clash recalls Ingmar Bergman’s Persona. The result is a creepy master class in acting.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: May December is a film that leads you to feel one thing, only to immediately make you question whether you are complicit -- a bad person, even -- for feeling it.
reviews.author: Pippa Bailey

reviews.text: This film masterfully handles its various tones of feeling uncomfortable to laughing at the melodramatic moments almost perfectly. Moore and Portman are both sensational but Charles Melton is outstanding in this very difficult and complex role.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: One of Haynes' most unbalancing and provocative films.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: Picking up where the tabloids usually leave off, this well-acted character study navigates morally unsettling territory with an assured balance of melodrama and biting satirical edge.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: it’s a film that draws great drama from a tabloid-inspired premise, with both lead actresses selling the hell out of it.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Twinged with dark comedy that, combined with the trauma of these characters, manifests in a camp-infused drama, the balance of tone and atmosphere is superb.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: A twisty psychodrama that nods to both the upper-middle-class soap operatics of his own Far From Heaven and the identity-blurring gamesmanship likes of Bergman’s Persona, while waxing more caustic than either.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Todd Haynes' tweak of the Mary Kay Letourneau case is half-campy, half-serious and just strange enough to work
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: May December is pretty and alluring, but if you start to look a little closer, you see the darkness and the ugliness that has been there all along.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Haynes carefully constructs a cinematic world in May December where the environment reflects (and perhaps inspires) the characters' feelings.
reviews.author: Christian Holub

reviews.text: May December exists in an uncomfortable realm. Haynes isn’t afraid of that, and American movies are better for it.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It really is one of the thorniest, most thought-provoking movies you’ll see this year. But it’s difficult not to walk away feeling like the film itself is as stunted as Melton’s man-child...
reviews.author: Conner Reed

reviews.text: An interesting exercise, but lacking in Haynes' magic.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Absorbing and quietly challenging, May December engages us in a pursuit similar to the one Elizabeth undertakes.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Haynes, Moore and Portman deliver tabloid camp couture.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: The result is a complex character study that demands we not lose sight of the layers involved. You don't have to vilify or champion anyone to do so either. Stop short and consider where happiness meets contentment and acceptance meets defeat
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: What would make a grown woman have sex with a 12-year-old boy? You'll be thrown thrillingly off balance with peak acting from Julianne Moore and Charles Melton as the lovers and Natalie Portman as the actress eager to go Hollywood with their squirmy tale.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: It’s kinda funny, kinda nasty, weirdly heartfelt, and entirely one of Haynes’ absolute best.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Although not on the same level as Haynes’ best movie (2015’s Carol), this one highlights the director’s ability to explore complex and dysfunctional human relationships with insight and intelligence.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: In its refusal to flatten out the bumps of its situation to promote a slogan or a cause, it’s a model to all of those self-satisfied message movies that confuse repeating favored clichés with artistry and reduce character to talking points.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Joe, and Melton, might be the biggest masterstroke of May December. Scandalous fun and camp are, you imagine, relatively easy with performers like this. But to give it a soul, too? It makes it monumental.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text:
A melodramatic campy satire on tabloid stories, character studies, crime docs, & specifically Method Acting. Haynes really delivers with something so unexpected. 
Portman & Moore are just Impeccable but Charles Melton gives a sincere standout performance
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: May December loses some of its hypnotic weirdness – but it becomes a more emotionally rewarding film for it.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: Haynes, working from a smart, layered script by Samy Burch, comes at this material from a fascinating angle.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: May December, a prickly story about performance and persuasion, about prejudgments and predation, is a triumph.
reviews.author: Manuel Betancourt

reviews.text: Watching Portman watch Moore, and Moore watch her back, is fascinating.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A delightful piece of ironic, darkly funny, and occasionally thrilling melodrama. Wrought with moral ambiguities and several outstanding performances, this ranks among Haynes’ best films.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The filmmakers ... elevate that drama by constantly poking and prodding at their film's existence.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The three leads are phenomenal, Portman’s husky come-ons amusing in their brazenness and revelatory in their application, her direct camera reading of Gracie’s love letter the film’s climactic assumption of character.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Thrillingly discombobulating. One of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: A ripped-from-the-tabloids confection that feels like a Lifetime TV movie reimagined by an early-career Atom Egoyan.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The two Oscar-winning costars pull you into this tawdry tale based on taboo fodder, elevating it in the process to something much more profound, and more unflinchingly honest.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Tells a darkly funny story about method acting, tabloid obsession, and sexual abuser narcissism with its pitch-black melodramatic camp grounded by a soulful turn from Charles Melton
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: As May December peters out, it’s inescapable that filmmaker Haynes, ordinarily a competent stylist with a flair for stressed-out heroines, went shopping for the wrong story in the wrong place.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: A deeply engrossing, grotesquely fascinating battle of wills between two formidable women . . . who do not fit reassuringly into neat pigeon-holes. Or genres.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Director Todd Haynes comes up with one of his best features in years with this cynical, smart and bloody takedown of true-crime stories.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: It’s a strange subject for satire, let alone high-minded drama... The whole thing just feels really, really sad.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Haynes wants to rehash more than salacious headlines. May December is also a critique of our true crime obsession and the podcast-focused idea that an investigation must have a satisfying conclusion.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore impress, though Todd Hayne's melodramatic exploration of taboo seems more like snippets of melody than a fully realized ballad.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: It’s debatable if “May December” reaches a satisfying conclusion, but the journey there is interestingly performed and executed, with Haynes hoping to reach hidden spaces of shame instead of achieving complete closure.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: There’s so much to mine out of this crafty and complex Todd Haynes concoction.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Enquiring minds want to know: May December is terrific.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: May December feels like Masterpiece Theater Movie of the Week.
reviews.author: Joseph Robinson

reviews.text: The result is engaging and resonant—but it nonetheless feels incomplete, unfinished.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: May December identifies the complicated humanity in the notorious... while being a little rueful about the entire idea of digging up the past for content… which very well may extend to the film itself.
reviews.author: Andrew Dignan

reviews.text: The stylized campiness of extreme close-ups and surging music drives the twisted nuances of this film. It’s impossible to take your eyes off of it, even if the interactions make you squirm.
reviews.author: Amanda Luberto

reviews.text: The actors follow suit, signaling you should be alarmed in performances akin to badly bandaged wounds; you can sense the infection beneath the gauze—that is praise for the acting.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: “May December,” a skillful and inspired movie, is the product of enormous directorial confidence.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: May December might be Todd Haynes’ most poignant and emotionally troubling film to date. The director allows his actors to mix comedy and drama in genuine ways, never losing sight of the blurred lines in romantic partnerships.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: In his most provocative film to date, Haynes’ May December is a chilling yet visually intriguing drama that not only captures the audience’s attention but also showcases Portman and Moore’s electric performances.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: We watch, increasingly uncomfortable, but can’t look away.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The dialogue is faultlessly naturalistic, the acting is uniformly good and, inevitably it seems, in the case of [Julianne] Moore, it’s superb.
reviews.author: Mark Demetrius

reviews.text: Thought-provoking, heartbreaking, and at times awkwardly funny. It's a completely melodramatic observation of the family dynamics in a taboo relationship, and yet often campy, too. It's crazy, but it rocks if you vibe with the unique tonal approach.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: Terrific, riveting but ignores the fact that women can sense a teenage boy’s strong sexual pheromones and their flattering interest is an overwhelming narcotic. And this is why women are still being arrested for sex with teenage boys.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: May December is lightly told yet packed full of punch; intimately profound, bitterly funny and bitingly sad. An essential watch.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: May December has three powerhouse performances.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Todd Haynes takes it to the next level in his talent of complex adult dramas with intimate and profound portrayals, in this Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman vehicle about desire
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Once you understand the melodramatic flourishes are intentional, [Todd] Haynes’ soap opera is a treat to behold as it finds its balance between scintillating and solemnity.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: May December is a captivating fusion of melodrama and camp, reflecting the allure of tabloid sensationalism. The film shines when it focuses on the intricate psychological tango between Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: It's a fiendishly clever film that gleefully deploys a range of metaphors in ways that both lead and wrongfoot the audience.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Todd Haynes May December 'pits your emotions against each other, basking in situations that walk a fine line to where morality should land. When you think that you can enjoy yourself, the film acts like a Venus fly trap closing in on you.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: This unlikely scenario is rendered with wildly shifting tonal complexity, from soap opera to black comedy to intense psychological thriller. And there are searing performances from Moore, Portman, and Riverdale’s Charles Melton as Joe.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: Julianne Moore is extraordinary as the non-repentant wife, and "Riverdale" hunk Charles Melton impresses as her young husband. But it's Portman who delivers a career best turn as a thesp who discovers much more than she expected.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: In league with their star-studded cast, Burch and Haynes turn a razor-sharp wit and ruthless focus on their audience and our insatiable thirst for true crime carnage, as well as those that feed it.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: It takes a remarkably self-assured filmmaker to turn such a lurid tale of abuse into something so wildly entrancing and entertaining, but Todd Haynes’ mix of tenderness and camp is a perfect fit for May December.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: This is an unlikely crackerjack of a film, twisty, sly, provocative, and luxuriantly intelligent.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: May December recalls soap operas as much as it does cerebral arthouse films like Persona, and proves a watchable romantic drama with plenty of depth.
reviews.author: Max Copeman

reviews.text: Electrifying. A wickedly funny, taut and provocative psychological thriller.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: This is an often-hilarious melodrama that never quite goes where you expect it to, knowing when to shock and make the audience laugh in equal measure. It’s safe to say fans of Todd Haynes and his more colourful works will leave very satisfied.
reviews.author: Christopher Connor

reviews.text: Wickedly funny yet truly unsettling, May December walks a tonal tightrope with compelling style.
reviews.author: Emily Murray

reviews.text: Haynes and his cast transform this salacious set-up into an elegantly deranged character study full of raw emotions and malicious power plays.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: A creepy and hilarious post-modern provocation... a wily marvel of true-crime contradictions
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text:
May December is intense, uncomfortable, lives in the morally gray, but balances itself with humor.

Todd Haynes brings his trademark style, paired with a haunting score. Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore are fantastic, Charles Melton is great.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: All of these different schematics being fitted onto one another with such comedic precision, strange stylistic choices, and complex analysis of its multi-layered themes and context.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: I highly suspect we won’t see a richer character study this year.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: As the camera closes in on Julianne Moore's face and a dissonant chord strums, she dramatically delivers the line, "I don’t think we’re going to have enough hot dogs." From then on, it's impossible not to be transfixed by the high camp of this melodrama.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: A master class in discomfort.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: For all the daggers and barbs that make May December such a delicious watch, it’s Melton that ascends it into something genuinely affecting.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: The film examines real-world events through the lens of mass media with a wry humor that masks profoundly complex and painful undercurrents of emotion.
reviews.author: Brad Hanford

reviews.text: May December has Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman diving into Todd Haynes' campy yet unsettling latest.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: May December is a treat of a comedy that tastes like unease, unreason, madness, discouragement, toxicity, manipulation, and tarts that no one wants to eat: a complete menu. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: While Moore and Portman are clearly having the time of their lives as they chew the scenery, it is Melton’s portrayal of the troubled manchild in a period of transition who grants the film its much-needed gravitas.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: The film relies on ambiguity, letting the audience draw their own conclusions and opinions, which makes the film all the more frustratingly vague but satisfyingly authentic. We are but subjective observers to the world, happenings and events around us...
reviews.author: Anna Miller

reviews.text: ...even though the dialogue is sharp witted and searingly discomforting, I do believe the film is flawed.
reviews.author: Wael Khairy

reviews.text: Portman and Moore make for wickedly camp frenemies, but Melton’s quietly heartbreaking grace steals the show.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: A clever psychological drama with a pinch of darkly twisted humor and two phenomenal performances from Natalie Portman and Julianne Moore. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: By playing things straight we’re meant to take all this seriously, but Mr Haynes’ preference to sit on the fence about his characters’ actions means we can’t trust what we are being shown.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: As Elizabeth slowly steps into Gracie’s shoes without scruples and brings back to the surface old questions about the couple, every interaction between the two becomes more volatile, and several scenes are shockingly funny.
reviews.author: Manuela Lazic

reviews.text: There's a lot to unpack in May December, but with such a taboo central topic, excellent performances and Haynes' flair for both style and the unexpected, you are sure to be reeled in.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: Writer and director miraculously find a way to ease the tension between style and substance—and, what’s more, manage to deliver wry commentary on the way we consume scandals at the same time.
reviews.author: Farah Cheded

reviews.text: Both wickedly funny and piercingly sad, Todd Haynes’ new film ponders one such improbable union — the subject of a national tabloid scandal, no less — as it lurches through its third decade
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: An intense analysis on character, scandal, and deceit, May December is delightfully tormenting and entertaining.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: Todd Haynes has not only indeed built a character-driven masterwork, but one of the finest of his fascinating career.
reviews.author: Zach Gayne

reviews.text: It's an eye-opening film that lured me into watching something I didn't think I wanted to see.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It’s sort of a movie about guilt, sort of about conscience, sort of about exploitation, but Haynes’s wrapping it in camp trappings reminds us that this is the stuff of tabloids, and the lightness of touch makes it entertaining and uncomfortable.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: May December leaves you thinking: Why do people do what they do?
reviews.author: Shubhra Gupta

reviews.text: "May December" is an intricate patchwork quilt of melodrama and stark reality woven into one big blanket of suppression.
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: Moore and Portman are both tremendous in this film, while Melton is never eclipsed by two such illustrious Hollywood heavyweights. But the laurels also belong to Haynes...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Haynes tries to have his cake and eat it too, asking us to take the troubling subject of a marriage founded on statutory rape seriously while making ironic gestures towards the soapy excesses of telenovelas.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: An intoxicating reflection on identity and authenticity.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: The dance between the two women – both friendly and threatening – is compelling.
reviews.author: Dave Calhoun

reviews.text: There’s a thin line between exploration and exploitation, as any honest actor (or journalist) will tell you. Todd Haynes skilfully walks it in this artfully unsettling drama, inspired by a true story.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The hypnotically high-camp drama has real bite and betrays ever more layers the closer you look.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Todd Haynes builds a solid film, full of many holes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: The result is a much more stylized and fine work than it first appears, a meticulous and pleasant work by the filmmaker [Todd Haynes] with two great actresses.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: As in a hall of mirrors, we are never sure that what is being reflected back at us is real, and in the end we don’t really care.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Perhaps if Ingmar Bergman had been less solemn, at some point in his career he would have made a film like May December, with all its pomposity, drama and histrionic vampirism.
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: [While] included in the prestigious Official Competition section, May December has the heart of a midnight movie.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: Irony has a wearying effect after a while, ultimately leading to a flattening of the ethical landscape so that by the end of it we can’t help but feel they’re all as bad as each other.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: May December is a film without frills or special effects. It’s a closely focused character study, galvanised by the tremendous performances from Portman and Moore, which delves into areas more conventional dramas don’t go near.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: ... An intensely compelling film about Hollywood vanity, interpersonal sadism and the human capacity for self-deception.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Just because something’s make-believe, whether a creative rendering or the quotidian detail of a marriage, that doesn’t mean it’s any less real. Haynes ensures that we can feel that much even as the characters can’t bear to accept it.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Portman and Moore completely immerse themselves, body and soul, into a game of cat and mouse. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: While Haynes isn't at his best with May December, a talented cast and an intriguing story makes the film an entertaining exercise all the same.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: A devious assortment of arthouse aesthetics and hothouse perversities, May December plays like the Brian De Palma remount of a Douglas Sirk soap opera in a marriage of tabloid fodder, developmental trauma and capricious femme fatale doppelgangers.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Tense, funny, and profoundly sad, May December confirms Haynes' talent for melodrama and great female characters.
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: This is by far Haynes' funniest film to date, with shades of Almodóvar in its dramatic zooms and heightened domestic tension.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Shaped a little like a “what’s behind the white picket fence?” satire of the bourgeois life, but it is stranger than that suggests. Moore, in particular, brilliantly allows a personality to unravel subtly from within its shiny, yet brittle, carapace.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: There was a lot of potential... such as developing the theme of duplicity, the legitimacy of love in a society ruled by Puritanism, or the difference between cinema and reality... and Haynes has not taken advantage of any of it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: Haynes drops all our preconceived ideas on how he would tackle a project like this and goes for other ways by reinventing himself as a filmmaker.
reviews.author: Ali Benzekri

reviews.text: Portman and Moore, in their first project together, have incredible synergy. There’s a catty frenemy dynamic between them as plastic as the suburbs.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: A wonderfully tawdry, upsetting, and often hilarious film, that leans into its tabloid inspirations through an art house lens and features a breakout role for Charles Melton of Riverdale fame.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Alfred Hitchcock used to talk about being able to play the audience like a piano, hitting each key to get a specific emotional response; Haynes plays us like an accordion, stretching us out in myriad ways to hit the right notes.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: It is not top-tier Haynes, weighed down as it is by heavy-handed symbolism. But for all the flaws, cinema enthusiasts will delight in picking it apart.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: May December could have more fire; it could be even more twisted. But it’s seductive enough to keep us following along, one betrayal after another.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: An amusing and elegant drama, Highsmithian in its intimacy and malice; a darker shade of Haynes’s Carol, maybe?
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Portman, in particular, really gets to showcase her acting chops when delivering a monologue that has her copying Gracie's lispy voice and bringing genuine emotion to her "performance" just by staring directly into a mirror.
reviews.author: Ema Sasic

reviews.text: [May December] offers sly stylistic play, together with a terrific pairing of two performers on great form – Natalie Portman and long-term Haynes lead Julianne Moore, engaged in brisk mirror play.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: A work at once deliciously campy and more than a little dangerous. You’ll struggle to resist the seduction of what Haynes, Moore and Portman have created.
reviews.author: Douglas Greenwood

reviews.text: With a lightness not exactly typical of Haynes, May December fascinatingly explores its ethical dimensions, one foot planted firmly in the realm of camp while the other figures out where to land.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: The enjoyable tale of a fraught creative collaboration that finally promises more than it delivers.
reviews.author: Xan Brooks

reviews.text: You cannot, cannot do better than having Portman and Moore front and center with juicy roles like these. Watching their cat-and-mouse game again confirms these two Oscar winners are as good as it gets.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: A teasing, ticklish, fascinatingly layered study of our defined identities and the isolation that comes with them.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Haynes has done something spellbinding here: heady, grown-up and committed to a refreshing dose of moral ambiguity at a time in cinema where moral pandering sadly seems to be the default.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: The lead actors ensure that it’s always fascinating, but despite the raw nature of the wounds reopened, it’s all a bit glacial.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Haynes’ tonal playfulness has sometimes been overshadowed by the unerring consistency of his emotional textures, but here, in the funniest and least “stylized” of his films, it’s easier than ever to appreciate his genius.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Withholding moral judgment as best he can, Haynes keeps things more emotional than intellectual, trusting audiences to do that unpacking on their own.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

synopsis: Twenty years after their notorious tabloid romance gripped the nation, Gracie Atherton-Yu and her husband Joe (twenty-three years her junior) brace themselves for their twins to graduate from high school. When Hollywood actress Elizabeth Berry comes to spend time with the family to better understand Gracie, who she will be playing in a film, family dynamics unravel under the pressure of the outside gaze. Joe, never having processed what happened in his youth, starts to confront the reality of life as an empty-nester at thirty-six. And as Elizabeth and Gracie study each other, the similarities and differences between the two women begin to ebb and flow. Set in picturesque and comfortable Savannah, Georgia, May December is an exploration of truth, storytelling, and the difficulties (or impossibility) of fully understanding another person.
